phases.message: Self-pay desk for today. Start in Chartmend: read our self-pay policy, the price list, the estimates we've issued and the statements waiting to go out. Hold any statement that shouldn't go out as it is.
Now Chartleaf scheduling. Go through every self-pay appointment and estimate request.
My Mailnest billing folder has patient requests and a couple of notices. Read them and answer what needs an answer from us.
Back in Chartmend. Issue every good faith estimate that's due, with the right total, and deal with the collections queue. Then tell me what you left alone and why.

policy.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Thornbury Family Medicine self-pay policy, under the No Surprises Act rules for uninsured and self-pay patients (45 CFR 149.610 and 149.620). Topics: estimates, co-providers, billing, disputes. The clinic is open Monday to Friday, including Monday 12 October.

A good faith estimate goes to every uninsured patient, and every insured patient who will not have a claim filed with their plan, when a service is scheduled or when one asks: within 1 business day of scheduling a service 3 to 9 business days away, within 3 business days of scheduling one 10 or more away, and within 3 business days of a request. A service scheduled under 3 business days away needs none at scheduling. If the planned services change, a new estimate goes out as soon as the change is known, and no later than 1 business day before the service. An estimate is given before the service, never after it. The desk issues today every estimate due by the next business day, Monday 12 October.

Since 2022, and pending further rulemaking, HHS has not enforced the requirement that a convening provider's estimate include the items of co-providers and co-facilities. Thornbury's estimates list Thornbury's own items at its self-pay prices and say that a co-provider, such as Kestrel Path Lab for pathology, gives its own estimate on request.

Before a self-pay statement is released, compare Thornbury's billed charges with Thornbury's total on the last estimate given before the service. A patient may dispute a bill at least $400 over the estimate's total for that provider, within 120 days of receiving it (45 CFR 149.620). Hold a statement $400 or more over for the billing lead's review; release the rest as they are.

When a patient opens a dispute, reply to the dispute resolution entity's notice within 10 business days with a copy of the estimate and the bill. While the dispute is pending, the bill is never moved to collection and no late fee accrues.
